findings.evidence: template/scripts/integration_contour.py:366-372 calls `first_record(...)` outside the `try`. That `try` catches only KeyError, TypeError and ValueError, and MalformedMarkerError is a RuntimeError (candidate_lifecycle.py:187). Before the change a malformed trusted record was skipped, and a missing record gave `None["at"]`, a TypeError that was caught and turned into JobBlocked. The new exception is not converted, so the caller gets an unclassified crash instead of a blocked job. The diff covers `_transition` and `worker` but not this caller.
findings.summary: A malformed trusted record now raises MalformedMarkerError out of `integration_contour.candidate_admitted_at`. The method's contract is that an unprovable start blocks with `JobBlocked`.

findings.evidence: publication_queue.py `_record_comment_id` (line 282) calls `latest_record` per comment. It is reached through `_earlier_slot_record` (lines 1005 and 1091) and `admit` (lines 1024, 1040, 1115). It is also reached through `_supersession` (line 897) and `_integration_repair` (line 1976). A single damaged trusted comment now propagates a bare RuntimeError subclass there. It is not a QueueError or LifecycleOwnershipChanged, so callers that catch those will not handle it. The design inventory says only that `_transition` and `worker` handle it.
findings.summary: Several publication_queue call sites that now raise MalformedMarkerError have no handling or mapping. This differs from the handling added in `_transition`, `_raise_if_owned_elsewhere` and `worker`.

findings.evidence: design.md, 'Malformed trusted records' decision, versus the new `class MalformedMarkerError(RuntimeError)` at template/scripts/candidate_lifecycle.py:187. The diff shows no existing class of that name.
findings.summary: design.md says a malformed trusted record raises 'the existing malformed-marker error'. The diff introduces a new `MalformedMarkerError` class in candidate_lifecycle.py, so the doc does not match the code.
